source_observations.evidence_summary: Official current faculty identity, education, Bell Labs postdoc, title, LBNL role and portrait.
LBNL biography explicitly identifies John Pople as the professor with whom Head-Gordon worked for his 1989 PhD and gives career-history context.

Institution-hosted joint interview explicitly states Martin and Teresa Head-Gordon are married, describes them as founders of CalSolv, names collaborations and visits, and discusses working as a scientific couple.
Public lab/group culture timeline with group photographs and outings from 2016-2024.
Current lab roster including role categories and several explicit co-advisor annotations.
Alumni roster with some current positions, useful for academic-lineage and career-transition graph construction.

collection_notes: The public spouse relationship is unusually well supported by an institutional joint interview and is appropriate for the PUBLIC_PERSONAL layer; avoid data-broker enrichment beyond that source.

A current group roster is evidence of membership in the Head-Gordon group, but co-advisor annotations mean it would be wrong to translate every listed member into an exclusive student-of-Martin relationship.

The sequence of group outing photographs is valuable for a lab-culture timeline and media presentation, but people should only be tagged as present when captions or another reliable source explicitly identify them.
Conference invitee lists and seminar circuits can generate derived co-presence/community edges, not automatic friendship or collaboration edges.
